headline: Vegas turns to Adin Hill after Carter Hart exits morning skate with injury
take:
Per ESPN, Vegas goalie Carter Hart left Tuesday's morning skate with an undisclosed injury, and Adin Hill will start against the Ottawa Senators instead. The Athletic's Jesse Granger posted that Hart "went down awkwardly, then limped off the ice here at morning skate."

Hill is a fair bet to hold the net, but neither goalie has been good so far this season. Our goals saved above expected, which measures how many goals a goalie stopped compared with what the quality of shots would predict, has Hill at -2.36 over five games (.882 save percentage) and Hart at -0.72 over eight (.889). Hill's -15.02 last season in 27 games is a reason for caution. The cost to VGK is real, since the team has been strong in front of its goalies, with 56.4% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, summed up) and 54% at five-on-five, yet its goaltending sits at -3.3 as a team. A goalie swap alone won't fix that. OTT, at 51.7% of expected goals, has had decent goaltending (+1.5), so this is a game where Vegas's edge in play could be eaten by whoever is in the crease.
